title: U.S. House · New York's 21st District
area: The North Country: St. Lawrence, Jefferson, Lewis, Franklin, Clinton, Essex, Hamilton, Fulton and Warren counties, plus parts of Saratoga and Herkimer counties in far northern New York.

context.text: This is an open seat. Incumbent Republican Elise Stefanik did not seek re-election to the House. She had run for Governor of New York but withdrew from that race on December 19, 2025.

Blake Gendebien defeated Stuart Amoriell in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, 64.5%-35.0%. Anthony Constantino defeated Robert Smullen in the June 23, 2026 Republican primary, 59.2%-40.3%; Smullen remains on the general-election ballot on the Conservative Party line.

summary.text: Blake Gendebien is a second-generation dairy farmer and small business owner from the North Country running as the Democratic nominee for this open seat; he won the June 2026 primary over Stuart Amoriell. He has not previously held federal office; his local roles include school board service and an agricultural cooperative board. His campaign focuses on affordability, healthcare access and government reform.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he was born and raised on a farm in the North Country and is a second-generation dairy farmer.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Pennsylvania State University in 1999.
Works as a farmer and small business owner; served as Vice Chair of the Cooperative Board of Agri-Mark.
Served as a member of the Lisbon Central School Board.
Describes himself as a JV basketball coach and founder of a nonprofit supporting children with pediatric cancer and their families.
Defeated Stuart Amoriell in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary for the open NY-21 seat, 64.5% to 35.0%.
Describes himself as a husband and father of three boys.

priorities.text: Affordability, including repealing what he describes as costly and unnecessary government regulations, supporting fair trade deals and bringing back American manufacturing to lower costs for working families.
Healthcare access in rural communities, including expanding telehealth, lowering prescription drug costs, and opposing cuts to Social Security, Medicare or Medicaid.
Government reform, saying he wants to end the "elected to lobbyist" pipeline and get dark money out of politics.
priorities.quote: I'm committed to cleaning up Washington and I will always be responsive to the voters of the North Country, not special interests.

positions.summary: Says he will protect a woman's right to choose and opposes new regulations imposing total abortion bans, including in cases of rape or when the mother's life is at stake.
Says he will never vote to cut Social Security, Medicare or Medicaid and wants to expand telehealth and lower prescription drug costs.

candidates.name: Anthony Constantino
candidates.currentRole: Founder and CEO of Sticker Mule

summary.text: Anthony Constantino is the founder and CEO of Sticker Mule, a printing and technology company based in Amsterdam, NY, running as the Republican nominee for this open seat. A first-time candidate who won the June 2026 primary over Assemblyman Robert Smullen with President Trump's endorsement, he describes his campaign as self-funded and centered on immigration enforcement, healthcare costs and government spending.

background.text: Founded Sticker Mule in Amsterdam, NY in 2010; WAMC reports it is now an international company employing more than 1,000 people. He describes himself as its founder and CEO.

In October 2024 he built a large "Vote for Trump" sign atop one of the company's Amsterdam factories overlooking I-90, which drew national attention, and emailed Sticker Mule customers urging support for Trump; he says the email cost the company revenue.
According to his Ballotpedia survey, he compiled a 2-1 professional boxing record (two knockouts) after turning professional for his 40th birthday.
Says he is fluent in Spanish and lists illegal immigration among the policy areas he is most passionate about.

Received President Trump's endorsement in April 2026 and was the only Republican in the primary to have it, according to WAMC; he had been described as a political outsider facing establishment Assemblyman Robert Smullen.
Defeated Robert Smullen in the June 23, 2026 Republican primary, 59.2% to 40.3%; Smullen remains on the ballot on the Conservative Party line.

priorities.text: Says he is self-funding his campaign to be free of special-interest influence and does not ask for donations.
Addressing illegal immigration, citing his fluency in Spanish and stating open borders have caused suffering in the U.S. and abroad.
Healthcare policy focused on innovation and outcomes rather than what he describes as an endless debate over making it free.

positions.summary: Cites illegal immigration as a top concern and says open borders have caused significant harm.

candidates.name: Christopher Schmidt
candidates.ballotNote: Write-in candidate on the general-election ballot

summary.text: Christopher Schmidt is an independent write-in candidate on the general-election ballot for NY-21 who completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, describing an independent, locally focused campaign.

background.text: Ballotpedia lists a Christopher Schmidt as a Libertarian candidate for NY-21 in 2018 who withdrew, and he declared as a write-in candidate for the November 3, 2026 general election. His Ballotpedia page contains no further biographical information.

priorities.text: Says his campaign focuses on local issues such as housing, healthcare access, and employment challenges in the region, an independent approach to legislation, and community engagement with residents' feedback.
priorities.quote: Focus on local issues: Highlights the importance of addressing housing, healthcare access, and employment challenges in the region.

priorities.text: Lists government accountability and transparency, housing and infrastructure, energy and utilities, economic and workforce issues, and healthcare access as the public-policy areas he is most passionate about.
priorities.quote: Government accountability and transparency: Emphasizing oversight, ethics, and public trust in institutions.

researchNotes: Christopher Schmidt (write-in) completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey (https://ballotpedia.org/Christopher_Schmidt_(New_York)), which supplied his priorities above; Ballotpedia's page for him has no separate biography section and lists no campaign website, so no background items or issue positions could be sourced. Federal key votes and FEC totals are added separately by script for sitting members of Congress; this is an open seat so no candidate has those. Biography gaps: Schmidt's public record contains no education, career or residence details; Gendebien's and Constantino's biographies rely on their own materials and a WAMC profile, and no full news profile of Gendebien was found.
